nodes.label: R3-REPAIR-PLAN — the 25 live-superseded findings as items to approve or refuse
nodes.rationale: A proposal, not a repair: each item names its site, what stands there, what the correction replaces it with, and a grade, so the decision is made once per item rather than once for the list.

nodes.label: The split is the corpus's own mechanic
nodes.rationale: Batch A is volume sites repaired in place by R3; Batch B is Register entries, and a Register entry is never edited — the repair is a new appended entry citing the superseded one.

nodes.label: A1 — the 2,475 self-contradiction
nodes.rationale: The volume prints its own withdrawal in one passage and asserts the withdrawn figure in two others; previously printed here is the tell that the edited passage was fixed and the others were not.

nodes.label: A3 — the closure rule is printed one-sided
nodes.rationale: Four volumes print an iff that register 402 has already corrected as two-sided; the widest-reach item, to be done with DEFERRED docket 9(a), which touches the same line for a different fault.

nodes.label: A5 needs a ruling before any edit
nodes.rationale: Register 1790 re-asserts the scope a repair would narrow while its own stage table gives Lambda-8 and Lambda-9 no cycle; this is the one item where repairing could put the volume in conflict with a later correction.

nodes.label: A8 is the item most easily over-repaired
nodes.rationale: The general claim survives and only its supporting evidence falls; a reader who repairs the headline would delete a result that stands.

nodes.label: B4 is not a repair at all
nodes.rationale: The file's one CORRECTION-SUPERSEDED row: Ruling 66 seated the genesis block flat, so the correction is the stale record and nothing in the Register changes.

nodes.label: B7 must not be worked
nodes.rationale: It is dockets 20x-04 / 20x-09, an outstanding Phase 0 ruling, and cypher.py's seated measurement puts statistics in the operator-bearing set — the correction B7 proposes is contradicted by the corpus's own instrument.
